editorial:
Imagine being a therapist who starts seeing scary things that aren't there. That is exactly what happens to Peter Bowers. He is already struggling with his own mental health, but things get weird when he notices his patients all have the same dark secret. The whole movie feels like a puzzle that you are trying to solve along with him. You will feel the tension build up as he travels back to his old hometown to face the things he tried to forget two decades ago. It has a creepy, moody vibe that keeps you wondering if Peter is actually losing his mind or if there is something truly evil hiding in his past.

The acting is solid and the twists keep you guessing until the very end. While some parts of the story move a bit slow, the payoff is worth the wait. If you love movies that mess with your head, you should definitely give this a try. You can grab a 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see all the dark details, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It looks great in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video if you have a big screen at home to make the scary scenes feel more real.
endingExplained: You find out that Peter was actually part of a cult as a child. The scary visions were memories of the rituals he went through. In the end, he discovers that the people from his past are still around and trying to bring him back into the fold. He has to fight off the cult members to finally break free from their hold on him. He survives the night and finally gets the peace he needs.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological puzzles and dark secrets.
